output.rationale: Teach membrane structure and transport as one bounded concept cluster, with one model block followed by self-explanation, repair, and reexplain checks.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because their hydrophobic interior lets some small nonpolar molecules pass more easily than polar or charged substances.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport requires energy to move them against the gradient.
completionEvidence: Explain why the phospholipid bilayer is selectively permeable.
Distinguish passive from active transport in a simple example.
Produce a corrected plain-language explanation after feedback.

methodBriefing.what: Study an accurate membrane model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining causes and relationships reveals missing links and builds a more usable mental model.
how: Study one concise model of membrane structure and transport.
Close it and explain the idea in plain language.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix the missing part.
Explain it again without copying the wording.

personalization: Use one concrete cell membrane example.
Keep the repair focused on the exact gap from your first response.

activities.label: Membrane model
activities.title: Membrane structure and movement
activities.body: Study the model and notice the two transport rules. Then continue to your own explanation.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because their hydrophobic interior lets some small nonpolar molecules pass more easily than polar or charged substances.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport requires energy to move them against the gradient.

activities.label: Explain it back
activities.title: Explain selective permeability
activities.body: In 2 to 4 sentences, explain why the membrane lets some substances cross more easily than others. Then state one transport example and whether it is passive or active.
activities.concept: Explain how phospholipid structure creates selective permeability
activities.correctAnswer: The phospholipid bilayer has a hydrophobic interior, so small nonpolar substances cross more easily than polar or charged substances. Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy, while active transport requires energy to move substances against the gradient.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the hydrophobic interior and links it to which substances cross more easily, then correctly classifies a transport example as passive or active.

activities.label: Fix the gap
activities.title: Repair the transport rule
activities.body: Revise your answer so it clearly separates energy-free movement from energy-requiring movement. Keep it to 2 to 3 sentences.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Confusing passive transport with active transport as if both require cellular energy or both move substances the same way.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
activities.feedback: The repair must clearly state that passive transport does not use cellular energy and active transport does use energy to move against the gradient.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: Explain the membrane again
activities.body: Explain both membrane ideas again in plain language, without copying the model. Include one example of a substance that crosses more easily and one example of transport that uses energy.
activities.correctAnswer: A membrane is selectively permeable because its hydrophobic phospholipid interior lets some small nonpolar substances cross more easily than polar or charged ones. Passive transport does not use cellular energy, but active transport does.
activities.feedback: A strong response restates both ideas clearly and keeps the transport distinction accurate in plain language.

activities.label: Quick check
activities.title: Membrane transport check
choices: Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without cellular energy.
Passive transport always requires ATP to move substances across the membrane.
Active transport never uses membrane proteins.
Active transport always moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without cellular energy.
activities.feedback: Passive transport is energy-free movement down a gradient. Active transport is the energy-requiring opposite case.

items.essentialIdea: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because hydrophobic tails block many polar solutes.

check.title: Phospholipid barrier function
check.prompt: How does phospholipid structure create selective permeability in a membrane?
check.referenceAnswer: The hydrophobic fatty acid tails form a nonpolar interior that blocks many polar molecules and ions, while small nonpolar molecules pass more easily.
check.feedback: Focus on the hydrophobic interior and which kinds of molecules it excludes.

items.essentialIdea: Passive transport moves substances down gradients without energy; active transport uses energy to move against gradients.

check.title: Passive versus active movement
check.prompt: How do passive transport and active transport differ in relation to concentration gradients and energy use?
check.referenceAnswer: Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against their gradient.
check.feedback: Keep the direction relative to the gradient and the energy requirement distinct.

recognitionCheck.title: Transport comparison
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes active transport from passive transport?
choices: Active transport uses cellular energy to move substances against a concentration gradient.
Active transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without energy.
Passive transport always requires ATP to cross the membrane.
Passive transport moves only ions through the membrane.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: Active transport uses cellular energy to move substances against a concentration gradient.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Energy use and movement against the gradient define active transport.
